2M.1 We are to give glory and praise unto God.

precepts.text: Worthy is the Lamb that was slain to receive power, and riches, and wisdom, and strength, and honour, and glory, and blessing. And every creature which is in heaven, and on the earth, and under the earth, and such as are in the sea, heard I saying. There are creatures in heaven, creatures on the earth, creatures created deep inside the earth nobody has ever seen, and creatures in the sea like leviathan that no man has seen. And they all heard, and they understood. The creatures understand us; remember the donkey talked to Balaam and asked him, why are you beating me?
precepts.point: But the redeemed shall walk there, and the ransomed of the Lord shall return, and come to Zion with songs and everlasting joy upon their heads. That is us walking back into our land.
precepts.why:
Isaiah says the wilderness and the desert shall be glad and “blossom as the rose.” When we are delivered, the desert places in our land will blossom and trees will start springing up, because we are connected to the earth. When the righteous people start ruling, everything changes. The animals are free, and the creatures understand us. That may sound like church talk, but the donkey did talk to Balaam: why are you beating me? Revelation shows how far that understanding goes.

“Worthy is the Lamb that was slain to receive power, and riches, and wisdom, and strength, and honour, and glory, and blessing.” Christ receives all these things.

“And every creature which is in heaven”: those are the angels. There are creatures in heaven. “and on the earth”: the animals created on the earth. “and under the earth”: creatures created in the earth, worms and such, and creatures living deep in the earth that nobody has ever seen. “and such as are in the sea”: leviathan, and creatures in the sea no human being has ever seen, that the Lord created. “and all that are in them”: everything that was created.

“heard I saying, Blessing, and honour, and glory, and power, be unto him that sitteth upon the throne, and unto the Lamb for ever and ever.” They heard what John said, and they understood it, all the creatures.

That is why the land itself rejoices in Isaiah 35. The whole creation answers to the Lord, and when “the glory of Lebanon” is given and they “see the glory of the Lord, and the excellency of our God”, it is because the Lord will be on the earth, and everything will change.

precepts.text: The Lion of the tribe of Judah, the Root of David, hath prevailed. That lion is Christ.
precepts.point: Habakkuk 3:16, the prophet's belly trembled because he was put in it, and when he cometh up unto the people he will invade them with his troops. Isaiah 31:4, like as the lion and the young lion roaring on his prey, the Lion of the tribe of Judah of Revelation 5:5, so shall the Lord of hosts come down to fight for mount Zion; as birds flying, Christ and the angels, he will defend Jerusalem, and passing over he will preserve it. Jeremiah 4:7, the lion is come up from his thicket, the destroyer of the Gentiles, Nebuchadnezzar contextually and Christ prophetically. 2 Esdras 11:37, a roaring lion chased out of the wood sends a man's voice unto the eagle, America.
precepts.why:
Isaiah says the Lord will come down to fight for mount Zion “Like as the lion and the young lion roaring on his prey”. Who is that lion? John shows it: “And one of the elders saith unto me, Weep not: behold, the Lion of the tribe of Juda, the Root of David, hath prevailed to open the book, and to loose the seven seals thereof.”

That lion is Christ, the Lion of the tribe of Judah, the Root of David. He is the one roaring on his prey, not afraid of the voice of the multitude of shepherds called against him, coming down with his angels as birds flying to defend Jerusalem. He is the mighty protection of them that love him.

precepts.text: The Lion of the tribe of Judah, the Root of David, has prevailed to open the book and loose the seven seals; this Lion goes into Christ.
precepts.point: Surely the Lord God will do nothing but he reveals his secret unto his servants the prophets. The lion has roared, who will not fear? The Lord God has spoken, who can but prophesy?

note.label: Amos 3: You Only Have I Known

precepts.why:
“The lion hath roared, who will not fear?” The lion goes into Christ: “behold, the Lion of the tribe of Juda, the Root of David, hath prevailed to open the book, and to loose the seven seals thereof.” Christ is the Lion of the tribe of Judah, the Root of David, who prevailed to open the book and loose the seven seals.

When that Lion has roared, who will not fear? The Lord God has spoken, and who can but prophesy?

precepts.text: Only the Lion of the tribe of Judah, the Root of David, prevailed to open the book and loose the seven seals.
precepts.point: "Restore" means to bring back and make new. The kingdom of heaven is Jerusalem and it always belonged to Israel, not to all nations; it is not pie in the sky when you die.

note.label: Acts 1: The Promise of the Father and the Kingdom Restored to Israel

precepts.why:
“Weep not: behold, the Lion of the tribe of Juda, the Root of David, hath prevailed to open the book, and to loose the seven seals thereof.”

The disciples did not yet understand the seven seals, because only the Lion of the tribe of Judah could open them. The book was not yet opened to them when they asked if the kingdom would be restored at that time. That understanding was given later to John, and now in these last days.

note.label: Why They Hated US: Walking in the Footsteps of the Persecuted

points: “And I saw in the right hand of him that sat on the throne a book written within and on the backside, sealed with seven seals.” There were seven seals on this book. Most of the seals have been done, so today we complete the seals, but that ain't the end of the series. Before Revelation 6, it is prefaced with the precept chapter, Zechariah 6.

This is John the Revelator on the island of Patmos, written around 96 AD; Patmos was a salt mine, a prison camp where Rome put some Israelites. “And I saw in the right hand of him that sat on the throne a book written within and on the backside, sealed with seven seals.” So there was a book that the Lord, the Father, held in his hand. As you read down it tells you that no man was worthy to break the seals off the book to bring forth judgment and wisdom, but then the Lamb came, which was Christ, and he began to break the seals off this particular book, and this particular book brought forth judgment upon the earth and understanding upon the earth.
